studyPlanSubmission.deadlineNote: There is no deadline, but you must fill in your study plan before you can register for exams on AlmaEsami.

keyDates.label: Classes, first term
keyDates.note: The programme officially starts on 14 September. The optional crash courses (no attendance required) start one week earlier, on 7 September.

keyDates.label: Re-sit exams
keyDates.note: There is one more re-sit session in September.

keyDates.label: Erasmus+ applications on AlmaRM
keyDates.note: Opens around the first days of January and closes by the first days of February. Check the exact dates on the UniBo Erasmus+ page.

keyDates.label: Summer School in Austria (one week)
keyDates.note: Right after the second semester. Attendance is strongly recommended.

keyDates.label: Thesis Guidelines sent to you
keyDates.note: In the summer before the second year.

keyDates.label: Re-enrolment deadline
keyDates.note: Register in Studielink and pay the fee. The payment deadline may change.

note.text: Crash courses are optional refreshers. They show 3 CFU on the UniBo course page, but they do not count towards the 120 credits of the degree.

modules.name: Introduction to Economics
modules.description: A short refresher on the core ideas of economics: how people and firms make choices, how markets reach equilibrium, and when markets fail.
modules.assessment: No final examination. Interactive classes; Pass/Fail outcome requires enrolment in the lecturer's recording session. The lecturer also requires Virtuale course enrolment.
textbooks: Mankiw, N. G. Principles of Economics. Cengage Learning (any recent edition).

assessmentNotice.virtualeInstruction: Enrol in the lecturer's Virtuale course. The lecturer specified a Tuesday-midnight deadline, but the shared email does not identify the calendar date; confirm it from the original message.
assessmentNotice.recordingInstruction: Enrol in the class named 'Esame Introduction to Economics (Crash Course)' created by the lecturer so that the Pass/Fail evaluation and corresponding credits can be recorded.
assessmentNotice.note: The lecturer confirmed no final exam, but did not explicitly guarantee automatic Pass for everyone. UniBo lists 3 CFU; the programme handbook treats optional crash courses separately from the 120 ECTS degree requirement.
assessmentNotice.source: Lecturer emails shared with the Student Hub · 2026/27

modules.name: Introduction to Management
modules.description: A short introductory (crash) course on management. The official course page hasn't been published yet.
modules.assessment: Not published yet. Check the official course structure.

courses.name: Fundamental in Health Economics and Management

modules.name: Fundamentals in Health Economics
modules.description: How economists analyse health and health care: why these markets are special, where they fail, how people demand care and insurance, and how governments and health systems respond.
modules.assessment: Closed-book written exam, 90 minutes. Grades on the 18–30 scale. More details are given in class.
textbooks: Bhattacharya, J., Hyde, T. & Tu, P. (2014). Health Economics. Palgrave Macmillan.
Sloan, F. A. & Hsieh, C.-R. (2012). Health Economics. MIT Press.
Folland, S., Goodman, A. C. & Stano, M. (2007). The Economics of Health and Health Care. Prentice Hall.

modules.name: Fundamentals in Healthcare Management
modules.description: Core management ideas and tools applied to health, pharma and biotech organisations, taught through lectures and group case studies.
modules.assessment: 50% in-class work (cases and presentations) and 50% final written exam (multiple choice and open questions). For non-attending students the exam counts 100%.
textbooks: Gomez-Mejia, L. R., Balkin, D. B. & Cardy, R. L. (2012). Management. McGraw-Hill.
Collis, D. J. & Montgomery, C. A. (2005). Corporate Strategy: A Resource-Based Approach (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.
Hill, C. W. Global Business Today (11th ed.). McGraw-Hill.

courses.name: Our Right to Health: Needs, Resources and Society

modules.name: Our Right to Health: Needs, Resources and Society
modules.description: An overview of health law with a focus on EU health law (economic freedoms, non-discrimination, human rights, values and ethics) and a comparison of Beveridge and Bismarck health systems.
modules.assessment: On-site written exam with multiple-choice and essay questions, for attending and non-attending students. No AI during the exam.
textbooks: Frischhut, M. (2026). What one should know about the European Union (EU): A quick introduction to EU law (5th ed.). NWV.
Greer, S. L. et al. (2024). Everything you always wanted to know about European Union health policy but were afraid to ask (4th ed.).

courses.name: Fundamentals of Quantitative Methods in Health and Healthcare

modules.name: Fundamentals of Statistics for Healthcare
modules.description: Describe healthcare data, model sampling and probability, estimate population parameters, build confidence intervals, and test means and proportions. Practical work uses Excel. Six syllabus topics are covered across 11 lectures and four exercise sessions.
modules.assessment: 90-minute computer-based written exam: 6 multiple-choice/short questions (35%), 2 statistical-output interpretations (30%), and 2 applied Excel exercises with Word answers (35%). Teacher-provided printed formula sheet, Excel-function list and statistical tables are permitted; personal notes, devices, web browsing, communication and AI tools are prohibited. Pass mark: 18/30. Check the syllabus and AlmaEsami for current arrangements.
textbooks: Rosner, B. (2016). Fundamentals of Biostatistics. Cengage.
Agresti, A. (2018). Statistical Methods for the Social Sciences (5th ed.). Pearson.
Plichta Kellar, S. B. & Kelvin, E. A. (2013). Munro's Statistical Methods for Health Care Research. Wolters Kluwer.

modules.name: Fundamentals of Econometrics
modules.description: The main tools economists use for empirical work: regression models and strategies to identify causal effects, so you can read and critically assess applied research.
modules.assessment: In-class quizzes, group problem sets and a final exam. Details on Virtuale. No AI during the final exam.
textbooks: Wooldridge, J. M. (2019). Introductory Econometrics: A Modern Approach (7th ed.).
Angrist, J. D. & Pischke, J.-S. (2014). Mastering 'Metrics: The Path from Cause to Effect. Princeton University Press.

courses.name: Quantitative Methods in Health and Healthcare

modules.name: Statistics for Healthcare
modules.description: Probability and statistics for analysing health data, from describing samples to hypothesis tests, plus a first introduction to regression and causal inference. Workshops use Stata.
modules.assessment: Written exam at the end of the course. AI tools are not allowed.
textbooks: Folland, S., Goodman, A. C. & Stano, M. The Economics of Health and Health Care, ch. 3 'Statistical Tools for Health Economics'.
Bertsekas, D. & Tsitsiklis, J. (2008). Introduction to Probability, ch. 1. Athena Scientific.
Altman, D. (1991). Practical Statistics for Medical Research. Chapman and Hall.

modules.name: Econometrics
modules.description: The linear regression model for cross-section and panel data: when estimates can be read as causal, with hands-on practice on real data in Stata.
modules.assessment: Quizzes, problem sets and a final exam. Details on Virtuale. No AI during the final exam.
textbooks: Wooldridge, J. M. (2019). Introductory Econometrics: A Modern Approach (7th ed.), chapters 2–8.

modules.name: Health Systems
modules.description: How health systems in OECD countries are organised, funded and reformed, compared side by side with their strengths and weaknesses.
modules.assessment: Presentation of an assigned reading plus a final written exam with open questions (the exam is two thirds of the grade). Without the presentation, a longer exam counts 100%. No AI during the exam.
textbooks: Toth, F. (2021). Comparative Health Systems: A New Framework. Cambridge University Press.

modules.name: International Law and Health
modules.description: The links between international law and public health: major health treaties and institutions (WHO, WTO, ILO, World Bank, UNAIDS) and how they shape health regulation and policy.
modules.assessment: Not published yet. Check the official course page.
